question: Can one modest open language model solve more ARC tasks by generating candidates efficiently and treating symmetry-transformed views as a product of experts at selection time?

key_findings.claim: The method uses ARC-valid transformations at three distinct stages: augmentation for fine-tuning, transformed views for candidate generation, and likelihood aggregation for candidate selection.
key_findings.evidence: Grid rotations/reflections, color permutations, and example reorderings are chosen to preserve a task's solution. A task-specific model is trained on augmented demonstrations, DFS explores token sequences, and the same model scores a proposed answer across sixteen transformed views by geometric-mean likelihood.

key_findings.claim: On the public ARC-AGI evaluation split, every major component contributes to the reported 71.6 percent two-guess accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: For the NeMo 8B configuration, Table 2 reports 18.3 for the base model, 44.5 after test-time training, 62.5 with sixteen-view sampling, 67.6 after product-of-experts selection, and 71.6 with DFS candidate exploration.

key_findings.claim: Product-of-experts scoring improves ranking rather than merely increasing candidate coverage, while DFS trades compute for higher-probability unique solutions.
key_findings.evidence: Table 3 separates the number of tasks for which a correct candidate was generated from the number ultimately selected. Multi-view log-probability aggregation selects correct candidates more often, and DFS reaches useful coverage with fewer redundant samples than naive stochastic decoding.

key_findings.claim: The headline result is a heavily ARC-specific public-split system result, not evidence that generic abstract reasoning has been solved.
key_findings.evidence: The pipeline uses hand-selected ARC symmetries, task-level fine-tuning, two allowed guesses, and extensive public-evaluation experimentation. It is not evaluated on the hidden ARC-AGI private set; ConceptARC and Sudoku provide useful but narrower transfer checks.

method.core_idea: Exploit solution-preserving perspectives of the same ARC task as conditionally independent experts, so agreement across views identifies robust candidate grids.
method.mechanism: A pretrained LLM is initially fine-tuned on ARC encodings and then adapted separately to each task's augmented examples. Depth-first search reuses prefix caches to enumerate high-probability outputs. Each candidate is transformed consistently with sixteen task views, scored by the adapted model, and ranked by pooled log likelihood before returning two guesses.
assumptions: Every chosen augmentation preserves the intended latent transformation and correct output distribution.
Likelihoods from transformed views provide complementary evidence despite being produced by one shared model.
Model likelihood is sufficiently calibrated to rank semantically correct grids.
Public ARC-AGI evaluation performance transfers to unseen task distributions and is not overfit through iterative method development.

techniques.role: Adapts the model to each puzzle using its demonstrations and transformations.
Generates multiple equivalent task perspectives for training, generation, and scoring.
Explores high-probability grid completions with less duplicate sampling.
Pools candidate likelihood across views to select transformation-consistent answers.

evaluations.setting: 400-task ARC-AGI public evaluation set with NeMo-Minitron 8B and a smaller Llama configuration.
evaluations.result: The full NeMo pipeline reaches 71.6 percent, with a monotonic ablation ladder from 18.3 percent base performance through test-time training, augmented sampling, PoE scoring, and DFS.
evaluations.baseline: Base fine-tuned model, test-time training alone, augmented stochastic sampling, and prior open ARC systems.

evaluations.setting: Candidate generation and selection ablation on the public evaluation tasks.
evaluations.metric: Correct-candidate coverage, selected accuracy, candidate count, and runtime.
evaluations.result: DFS and multi-view scoring improve the coverage-to-selection conversion; the reported average inference cost is approximately two cents per task under the authors' GPU-price assumption.
evaluations.baseline: Naive stochastic sampling and single-view likelihood selection.

evaluations.metric: Two-guess/top-one accuracy and whether a correct sampled Sudoku is selected.
evaluations.result: The system reports 73.3 percent on ConceptARC and 53 percent top-one Sudoku accuracy; when a correct Sudoku appears in the candidate set, the selector chooses it in the reported cases.
evaluations.baseline: Sampling without PoE-style selection and task-specific prior results.

limitations: The primary score is on the repeatedly visible public ARC-AGI evaluation set, not the hidden private set.
The pipeline relies on hand-engineered ARC symmetries, encodings, and task-level fine-tuning.
The product-of-experts interpretation treats correlated views from one model as if they contribute distinct evidence.
Runtime and price claims depend on specific hardware, caching, stopping thresholds, and a low assumed GPU hourly cost.
failure_modes: A transformation believed to preserve the rule can alter a puzzle with directional or color-semantic structure.
If no correct candidate is generated, likelihood aggregation cannot recover one.
Overconfident probability on a wrong but view-consistent grid can dominate the product.
Task-specific fine-tuning can overfit the few demonstrations or become unstable after an erroneous synthetic target.
reusable_insights: Apply known invariances not only as training augmentation but also as a test-time consistency ensemble.
Separate candidate coverage from candidate ranking when evaluating reasoning systems.
Prefix-cached structured search can turn an autoregressive model into a practical discrete program enumerator.
open_questions: How much of the public-set gain survives a frozen, previously unseen ARC-AGI test?
Can transformations be inferred and verified automatically rather than supplied as ARC-specific prior knowledge?
Would independently trained experts provide better-calibrated evidence than correlated views of one model?

competitive_landscape.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Test-Time Training for Abstract Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Establishes per-task test-time training as a strong open ARC-AGI strategy and is a direct system baseline.
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper adds cached DFS candidate generation and product-of-experts scoring across transformations on top of task adaptation.

competitive_landscape.title: Tackling the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus with Vision Transformers: The Importance of 2D Representation, Positions, and Objects
competitive_landscape.relationship: Develops an ARC solver whose architecture and representation preserve two-dimensional grid structure.
competitive_landscape.difference: It modifies the learned representation and vision architecture; the present work retains an autoregressive LLM and improves adaptation, search, and view-consistent ranking.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Measure of Intelligence
competitive_landscape.relationship: Introduces ARC and its theory of skill-acquisition efficiency as a target for general intelligence evaluation.
competitive_landscape.difference: It defines the benchmark and conceptual objective; this paper constructs a highly engineered solver for the grid tasks and does not validate the broader intelligence measure.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Transformation-pooled product-of-experts selection plus DFS exposes latent ARC ability in modest open LLMs at low cost.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Component ablations attribute measurable public-set gains to PoE ranking and DFS beyond test-time training and augmented sampling.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The integration and careful coverage-versus-selection ablation are useful, but the novelty is primarily systems composition and its generality remains uncertain without hidden-set replication.
